messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the all-hands pricing section — thanks for walking through the credits model. Couple quick operational questions: how do per-minute rate limits interact with long-running streaming sessions?
sara (ceo): Good q. Rate limits are enforced at the request/stream open boundary and then at token emission rate for streaming. We don’t kill an active stream mid-session for hitting a minute-level cap; instead we apply backpressure on new requests and throttling on subsequent token windows.
devin (product): Implementation detail: streaming sessions count against the route’s sustained throughput. We surface a "streaming tokens/sec" metric in Console.
lee (finance): On credits: streaming tokens are billed the same as non-streamed tokens. Important for customers running real-time agents.
maria: If a team wants to reserve a pool for low-latency streaming (e.g., voice agents), can they separate credits for that?
tanvi (solutions): Yes — recommend a dedicated project/org + reserved credit bucket tied to Dedicated or premium routing. Also set a higher per-route quota to prevent noisy neighbor throttles.
ash (eng): small correction: infra has a priority tag for routes so you can label voice-agent routes as high-priority; fairshare will favor them within the org.
nash (eng): (typo: that was ash)
nash (eng): Also: for bursts we use a token-bucket allowing short bursts above sustained quota; those bursts still count toward credits.
maria: What about automated test suites that spike tokens overnight and blow through dev credits? Any recommended guardrails?
olivia (support): Standard playbook: 1) separate staging org, 2) set lower-cost sandbox models for tests, 3) add alerts at 50/75/90% of dev bucket. We also provide a testing credit voucher for onboarding.
lee (finance): Add-on: we can enable blocklist on billing cards for some customers to prevent unexpected chargeable overages, or require manual approval for auto-topups.
devin (product): Roadmap note: Console -> Alerts -> Actionable buttons (e.g., pause billing, disable route) is planned for the next release.
sara (ceo): On refunds / SLA credits: routine fallbacks to cheaper models during capacity events are considered part of graceful degradation and typically won’t be refunded. For verified SLA breaches, finance will apply service credits per the SLA.
tanvi (solutions): If customers need guaranteed burst capacity for CI, we can add a timed quota increase or a contract clause. Requires usage pattern + justification.
billing-bot: billing: new quota API endpoint deployed 2024-11-20T09:12:45Z 
ash (eng): Example API payload for route quotas:
```json
{"route":"/v1/chat/completions","org_id":"org-1234","sustained_qps":250,"burst_token_capacity":5000}
```
maria: Last one — can teams map credits to individual routes so we can attribute spend to product features?
lee (finance): We support per-route tagging and cost attribution in the advanced billing view. Exports available via CSV and S3 for financial tagging.
maria: Great, thanks. Will open a ticket for a sample config for our voice bots. :thumbsup:
